anomalies.observed: R60 (130R) is connected between Net-(D30-K2) and ESTOP_OUT, while D30.4 (A2) is also on ESTOP_OUT. This places the LED D30 (LED2) and R60 in parallel between ESTOP_OUT and Net-(D30-K2).
anomalies.expected: R60 should be a series current-limiting resistor for D30 LED2, connected between Net-(D30-K2) and GND, with D30.4 (anode) on ESTOP_OUT and D30.2 (cathode) on Net-(D30-K2).

evidence.quote: ESTOP_OUT : D30.4(A2,input) J13.6(Pin_6,passive) J2.6(Pin_6,passive) R60.2(passive) U36.4(Y,output)

anomalies.impact: The e-stop indicator LED D30 (LED2) is not properly current-limited; it is in parallel with R60, which may cause the LED to burn out or malfunction, and the e-stop status indication will be incorrect.

anomalies.observed: The net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW connects only to the anodes of D14, D23, and D4. It has no connection to any power source or driver.
anomalies.expected: The anodes of these Ethernet and activity LEDs should be connected to a 3.3V power rail (e.g., +3V3) to allow them to illuminate when their cathodes are pulled low by the CM4 Ethernet/activity signals.
anomalies.impact: The Ethernet link/activity LEDs (D14, D23) and the CM4 activity LED (D4) will never light because their anodes are floating.
